content:
Today's operating system updates released by Apple contain a large number of security fixes, with technical details showing that AI tools are rapidly becoming part of vulnerability research. Details are as follows.

AI tools credited in Apple's latest update

Apple recently released:

  • iOS 26.6
  • iPadOS 26.6
  • macOS Tahoe 26.6
  • macOS Sequoia 15.7.8
  • macOS Sonoma 14.8.8
  • tvOS 26.6
  • visionOS 26.6
  • watchOS 26.6

Following the release of the updates, Apple promptly updated its security release page to provide more information on several fixed issues, including the affected components and devices, potential impact, patches, and a list of researchers who reported the issues.

One noteworthy detail in this documentation is its considerable length, especially considering Apple only released the 26.5.2 update a month ago, stating it already contained fixes originally planned for the 26.6 cycle.

Another noteworthy detail is that Anthropic researchers and Claude received credit for fixes related to WebKit, WebKit Storage, and WebDAV, some of which were completed jointly with researchers from Calif.io.

It was this same research team that announced in May this year that they used Anthropic's Mythos Preview model to construct a working macOS kernel memory corruption exploit on the M5 chip in just five days.

Calif received credit for multiple kernel security fixes across all operating system updates released today, with more than ten other researchers also credited, reflecting that multiple teams independently reported the same underlying vulnerabilities.

In fact, Apple also fixed a large number of other kernel vulnerabilities in this release cycle, with today's operating system updates collectively listing 30 different CVEs.

Also worth noting is that Apple has had access to Claude Mythos Preview through Anthropic's "Project Glasswing" program since April this year. Therefore, the number of vulnerabilities discovered internally using Claude may be higher than what is reflected in public credits.

Finally, Anthropic is not the only AI company in this update's credits. Apple also credited work involving OpenAI's Codex Security, Z.AI's GLM, and NVIDIA's AI Red Team.

Although some names also appeared in last month's security bulletins, this update further demonstrates just how quickly AI-assisted security research is evolving, and companies will need to quickly adjust their update schedules (as well as bug bounty programs) to adapt to this new reality.
